lawyer:
Rais Uddin Ahmad, Advocate-For the Petitioners. 
Md Mostafa Kamal Advocate—For the Respondent No.2.
parties:
Technomech Engineering (Pvt) Limited and another ------ Petitioners
vs
Judge, Artha Rin Court No. 2, Dhaka and another ------  Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Ashfaqul Islam J: At the instance of the petitioners, this Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why Order No. 127 dated 14-6-2011 passed by respondent No. 1 in Artha Rin Suit No. 1 of 2011 rejecting application of petitioners under Sections 57, 45 and 22 of the Artha Rin Adalat Act 2003 for appointment of Mediator under Section 22 of the said Act to settle the matter between petitioners and Bank through mediation (Annexure-G) and order to proceed with the proceedings of Artha Rin Suit No.  1 of 2011 without affording opportunity to petitioners to settle the case through mediation as per law should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 "The petitioner No. 1 is a private limited company and the petitioner No. 2 is the Managing Director of petitioner No. l. The petitioner No. 2 in course of his business obtained different loans from the respondent No. 2 Sonali Bank Limited (hereinafter referred to as Bank) and ultimately became a sick industry. The bank filed Artha Rin Suit No.  92 of 2001 which was renumbered as Artha Rin Suit No. 1 of 2011. The suit was contested by the petitioners. It has been stated in 'paragraph 6 of the petition that due to various proceeding in the lower Court the case could not proceed on for about 10 years and eventually Artha Rin Suit No.  92 of 2001 was reopened upon transfer at the Court of respondent No. 1 wherein it was renumbered as Suit No. 1 of 2011. The reasons for which the case could not proceed have been detailed in paragraph 4 and 5 of the petition. It has been further stated that petitioner being a sick industry could not settle the dues with the Bank. In the course of event the case was ultimately dismissed and the petitioner thereafter filed an application before the respondent No. 1, Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka under sections 57, 45 and 22 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 on 14-6-2011 praying for settlement of the suit through mediation under the provision of section 22 of the Ain and the said application being rejected by order No. 127 dated 10-6-2011 the petitioners moved this Division and obtained the present Rule and order of stay. 

 "That the real facts of the case, is that, the Artha Rin Suit case No.  92 of 2001 was filed on 12-4-2001. Subsequently Renumbered as Artha Rin Suit No.  1 of 2011 and after hearing both the parties, the said case was fixed on 8-7-2003 for Judgment but the writ petitioners filed writ petition No.  5064 of 2003 on the grounds of sick Industries and obtained stay order there under, which was discharged on 3-5-2007 against that petitioners preferred Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.  667 of 2007 and obtained stay order there under, which was ultimately discharged. Thereafter, Learned Judge on 31-3-2008 and 15-4-2008 respectively fixed for Judgment but writ petitioner again filed another writ petition being No.  2044 of 2007 and obtained stay order, which was eventually discharged; that again petitioners preferred another Civil Petition for leave to Appeal No.  243 of 2009 but no stay order was there. In such way, petitioners on the plea of it took several adjournments to delay the case. Lastly, on 24-9-2008 fixed for judgment and petitioners on that day filed transfer Misc. Case. Later on 11-4-2010 petitioners filed an application to settle the matter outside the Court (ADR) and learned Judge accordingly allowed the same but the petitioners did not present in the ADR though the respondent Bank was present there. Again, petitioners on 29-7-2010 sought ADR. In this way, petitioners travelled up to the all Artha Rin Courts below by filling several applications in a various way to delay the case. That the order dated 23-5-2011 passed by the learned District Judge, Dhaka, notice issued by the petitioners learned advocate and application dated 23-3-2011. 

 6. The moot question that faces this Division in this petition is whether under the facts and circumstances of the case the order impugned against has been passed in gross violation of the mandatory implication of section 22 of the Ain. 

 7. By now it has been settled that after the amendment of section 22 of Ain more so when it is read together with section 24 of Ain it becomes clear that the mediation has been made mandatory on the part of the Court itself, that is to say that at the initiation of the Court it has to be proceeded even if no steps have been taken on behalf of either sides. No one denies the said proposition of law. But the facts are totally different in the case in hand. If we glean the facts, it transpires that back in the year 2001 the suit was filed which could not proceed due to various proceedings arising out of the suit as already mentioned above and the suit was ultimately dismissed. The petitioner on 29-4-8 filed transfer Miscellaneous case wherein on 11-4-2010 he filed an application to settle the matter outside the Court and the Adalat accordingly allowed the same but the petitioner thereafter did not appear in the ADR though the respondent-bank was present. Again on 29-7-2010 the petitioner sought for ADR. In this way the petitioner filed applications after applications on different pretext and finally on 14-6-2011 it resulted in the passing of the impugned order. 

 9. As we have mentioned already that, the amended section 22 of Ain has certainly made it obligatory on the part of the Court to direct mediation. There is no question about that. But to get advantage of section 22 one should come with clean hands. In the case in hand as we have found from the conduct of the petitioner that from the very beginning he ventured on different pretext only to delay the proceedings of the suit. We have found the reflection of the same in the affidavit-in-opposition filed by the respondent-bank as mentioned above. The yardstick of evaluating and interpreting a law should always be founded in an equitable basis and no one can be allowed to achieve something indirectly which in law he cannot achieve directly. It can also be said that by twisting the simple meaning of law it cannot be used for taking a benefit, which in real sense of the term goes against the essence of law itself. We are absolutely in respectful agreement with the proposition that the amended section 22 of Ain itself is binding upon the Court that is to say that the Court has to take initiative for mediation, of course in a fit case. But in the case in hand we do not see that the principle and purport of law has any manner of application.
